clue.text: High-level meeting? Problem with it being disrupted by millions

indicators.note: something disrupted is broken into, so the pair of words is split open to admit another letter

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem set in school
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A puzzle-solver's complaint: a problem becomes harder once millions of something get mixed into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being disrupted by' puts the millions letter between the two joined pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of heads of government is called a summit, literally the highest level; the question mark flags the pun on 'high'.

clue.text: Resentment, not originally speechless anger

indicators.note: not originally means without its first letter

parts.note: dumb means unable to speak, speechless
rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: Resentment shows itself as anger that is not, at first, wordless.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence, so it is a feeling of resentment.

clue.text: Single bit of money will support factory girl

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting pieces sit below, so they follow the factory word

parts.note: a mill is a factory, as in a cotton mill
I, the Roman numeral one, means single
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: A single coin will be enough to keep a factory girl going.
explanation.definitionFit: Millicent is a girl's first name, so it fits the bare word by example.

clue.text: Trace of contamination from certain toxins

indicators.note: from means the letters are drawn out of the following words

explanation.surface: A lab finds a trace of contamination from certain toxins.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a slight trace of something polluting or corrupting.

clue.text: Unexpectedly meet tramp with piebald horse

parts.note: a bum is a vagrant or tramp, chiefly in American usage
a pinto is a horse with patchy markings, a piebald

explanation.surface: A rambler happens upon a vagrant leading a patchy-coated horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to encounter someone by chance, matching an unplanned meeting.

clue.text: Supporting acts maybe not seen publicly

parts.note: to be behind someone is to support them
plays divide into acts and scenes, so acts are an example of such divisions

explanation.surface: Support acts at a concert are not seen by the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporting acts' looks like a single phrase about warm-up bands but splits into two pieces; 'maybe' marks acts as one example of stage divisions.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in private, out of public view, from the backstage area of a theatre.

clue.text: A port for the PM

definitions.meaning: a major port city in Victoria, Australia
Lord ... was Queen Victoria's first Prime Minister

explanation.definitionFit: The Australian city and the Victorian statesman share this name; the city was named after him.

clue.text: River in northernmost part of Delaware, America

indicators.note: in a down clue the northernmost part is the top, the first letter

explanation.surface: A river in the northern part of the US state of Delaware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but supplies IN. America gives US.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a great river flowing through Pakistan, named here by its category.

clue.text: Solitary sort mislaying old part of rigging

indicators.note: to sort letters is to arrange them into a new order
mislaying means losing, so a letter is taken out

explanation.surface: A solitary kind of person keeps losing an old part of a ship's rigging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' looks like a noun but signals an anagram of SLITARY, SOLITARY without O.
explanation.definitionFit: A trysail is a small fore-and-aft sail used in rough weather, so part of a ship's rig.

clue.text: Singer getting break, appearing on theatre poster namely

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece appearing on another sits after it, so the break follows the poster and namely

parts.note: a playbill or bill is a printed theatre poster
i.e. (id est) means namely
a holiday is a break from work

explanation.surface: A performer gets her big break, her name now printed on a theatre poster.
explanation.walkthrough: Billie Holiday was the American jazz singer nicknamed Lady Day.
explanation.definitionFit: She was a celebrated jazz vocalist, so a singer is an apt general description by example.

clue.text: Scottish town showing American in Paris?

indicators.note: one piece set in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: Paris Hilton, the American socialite, gives her surname; the question mark flags a definition by example

explanation.surface: A Scottish town is said to have the air of an American visitor to the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris looks like the French city, but it is the first name of Paris Hilton; AM goes inside her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamilton is a large town in South Lanarkshire, south-east of Glasgow.

clue.text: Unusually large Welsh woman, narrator of poem

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for unusually large sizes
Sian is a common Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: An unusually large Welsh woman narrates a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Ossian is the legendary Gaelic bard credited as narrator of James Macpherson's 18th-century epic poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Macpherson presented his poems as translations sung by this ancient bard, who is their narrator.

clue.text: Complaint by thespian about new 'angel'

indicators.note: the complaint word goes about, around, the letter for new

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint
a thespian is an actor

explanation.surface: A grumble by an actor about a new 'angel' backing the show.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre slang an angel is a financial backer of a production, i.e. a patron or sponsor.

clue.text: Advise sparkling wine with an hors d'oeuvre assortment

parts.note: to tip is to give advice, as in tip someone off
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A waiter suggests serving sparkling wine with an assortment of starters.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay order is AN, TIP, ASTI; 'with' is only a joiner.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are a mixed Italian starter, a selection of cold meats and vegetables.

clue.text: Greasy piece of lace daughter dropped

indicators.note: something dropped is left out, so a letter is removed from the lace word

parts.note: a doily is a small ornamental lace mat

explanation.surface: A daughter drops a greasy piece of lace.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something coated with or containing fat or oil.

clue.text: Row behind back of steamer in choppy ocean, as a rule

indicators.note: in means set inside the jumbled letters
choppy water is rough and broken, so the word ocean is broken up
the noise word comes behind, after, the vessel's final letter
back of the vessel's name means its last letter

parts.note: a din is a loud noise, a row

explanation.surface: A rowing boat trails behind a steamer in a choppy ocean, as is usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like rowing but means a noise; 'choppy' gives OANCE, which takes in the rest. 'As a' is a joiner.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative decree or regulation, which is a rule.

clue.text: Note Carpenters' first success

indicators.note: first of the band name means its opening letter

parts.note: a hit is a success, especially a popular record

explanation.surface: A note about the pop group the Carpenters' first hit record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like music; it is the definition, a short written note.
explanation.definitionFit: A chit is a short note or voucher, such as a signed slip for a debt.

clue.text: Leader had name changed

indicators.note: changed signals the letters altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A leader has had their name changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A headman is the chief of a village or tribe, its leader.

clue.text: Great Tudors out to recruit English soldiers

indicators.note: recruiting takes others in, so the jumbled letters enclose the rest
out signals the royal dynasty's name put out of order

parts.note: men is a common word for soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: The Tudor monarchs set out to recruit English soldiers, a great undertaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' rearranges TUDORS into TRDOUS, which takes in E and MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean very large or impressive, as in a great or enormous effort.

clue.text: Ineffective advice for drug addicts?

definitions.meaning: taken as two words it urges taking smaller amounts

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into two words of advice about consumption.
explanation.definitionFit: Something futile or of no value is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Region to the west occupied by a governor once

indicators.note: occupied by means the reversed letters hold another inside
in an across clue going west means reading leftwards, backwards

parts.note: parts means a region or area, as in these parts

explanation.surface: A region to the west was once occupied and run by a governor.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTS reversed is STRAP, which A splits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in the ancient Persian empire, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Equestrian's condition

definitions.meaning: a clause added to an agreement, a proviso

explanation.walkthrough: 's is read as 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rides a horse, and an added stipulation attached to a document.

clue.text: Given permanent position, replacement editor's content

indicators.note: the content of the words means letters held within them

explanation.surface: A replacement editor is happy to have been given a permanent post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like 'happy' but means contents; the answer runs across 'replacement editor's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cemented is to be fixed firmly in place, made permanent.

clue.text: Film shows military leader taking over less than half of Vietnam

indicators.note: the leader-and-over group takes the Vietnam letters on board, so they follow on after it
a leader of a word is its first letter, here of military

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: the country's name has seven letters, so fewer than half keeps only its opening three

explanation.surface: A war film features a military leader taking over part of Vietnam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Military leader' looks like a commander but just gives M; 'taking' is a joiner.
explanation.definitionFit: Movie is the everyday American word for a cinema film.

clue.text: Keen on a place to meet round island in part of New York

indicators.note: round means the keen-on words go around the island letters

parts.note: to be mad on something is to be keen on it
a venue is a place where people meet

explanation.surface: Someone keen on a meeting place near an island in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Madison Avenue is a Manhattan street, a part of New York known for advertising.

clue.text: Smartphones misused by dad? No sir!

indicators.note: misused letters are put to the wrong use, set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A child refuses to let Dad loose on modern smartphones, which he misuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Android is Google's phone operating system, so these are phones running it, by metonymy.

clue.text: Nevertheless, church service is only three-quarters complete

indicators.note: eight letters only three-quarters complete keeps six, losing the final quarter

parts.note: evensong is the evening church service in the Anglican church

explanation.surface: Nevertheless, the church service ended early, only three-quarters done.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are concessive expressions meaning despite that, all the same.
